english.title: Intentionally obstruct the exercise of a right conferred by a warrant under s.176 Financial Services and Markets Act
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), intentionally obstructed the exercise of a right, namely **(..SPECIFY THE RIGHT..) conferred by a warrant under section 176 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000
english.legislation: Contrary to section 177(6) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the 'appropriate regulator' (either the Financial Conduct or the Prudential Regulation Authority) or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
